target_posture.statement: Target selection remains a governed later decision; this milestone inventories the source and migration risks without claiming a completed mapping.

workloads.business_question: Can customer and account behavior move from Oracle-owned service schemas without changing identifiers, balances, lifecycle dates, constraints, or API behavior?

migration_risks.name: Service-owned schema boundary
migration_risks.statement: The account and customer services own separate Oracle schemas and Liquibase change logs; a target must preserve ownership and deployment order.

migration_risks.name: Oracle identity generation
migration_risks.statement: NUMBER identity columns with START WITH and CACHE semantics require an explicit target identity policy.

migration_risks.name: Money and date semantics
migration_risks.statement: Unscaled NUMBER balances and Oracle DATE/SYSDATE behavior require bounded precision, timezone, and default-value decisions.

migration_risks.name: Constraint and ORM behavior
migration_risks.statement: Primary keys, foreign keys, checks, uniqueness, JPA mappings, and repository queries must be compared at schema and API levels.

workloads.name: Customer and account management

workloads.business_question: Can transfers retain debit, credit, compensation, journal, and failure behavior after the Oracle persistence layer is replaced?

migration_risks.name: LRA coordination
migration_risks.statement: The transfer service starts an Oracle MicroTx LRA and invokes account participants; the target must preserve coordination and termination semantics.

migration_risks.name: Compensation state machine
migration_risks.statement: Complete, compensate, status, and after-LRA callbacks form a durable state machine that cannot be reduced to successful HTTP responses.

migration_risks.name: Local transaction boundaries
migration_risks.statement: Participant callbacks combine distributed coordination with local Spring transactions and require atomic journal and balance behavior.

migration_risks.name: Journal idempotency
migration_risks.statement: LRA identifiers and journal states must survive retries, duplicate callbacks, cancellation, and recovery without double application.

workloads.name: Money transfer

workloads.business_question: Can asynchronous cheque deposit and clearance retain delivery, ordering, authorization, retry, and balance-update behavior on a new database?

migration_risks.name: Transactional Event Queue
migration_risks.statement: The workflow uses Oracle Transactional Event Queue/JMS configuration whose delivery contract requires a target messaging decision.

migration_risks.name: Delivery and replay
migration_risks.statement: Deposit and clearance consumers must retain acknowledgement, retry, duplicate-delivery, and replay behavior.

migration_risks.name: Internal service authorization
migration_risks.statement: Cheque consumers call protected account endpoints with service identity; database migration must not weaken that boundary.

migration_risks.name: Event-to-balance consistency
migration_risks.statement: Pending journal creation and later clearance form an eventual-consistency contract that needs end-to-end comparison.

workloads.name: Cheque deposit and clearance

workloads.business_question: Can Oracle-backed user storage move while preserving OAuth2/OIDC issuance, scopes, ownership checks, credential protection, and audit behavior?

migration_risks.name: User repository schema
migration_risks.statement: Oracle identity columns, VARCHAR2 character semantics, TIMESTAMP/SYSDATE defaults, uniqueness, and audit columns need target mappings.

migration_risks.name: Audit trigger semantics
migration_risks.statement: An Oracle editionable trigger derives update identity through SYS_CONTEXT and REGEXP_SUBSTR; equivalent audit behavior must be designed explicitly.

migration_risks.name: OAuth scope boundary
migration_risks.statement: APISIX and each service independently enforce CloudBank scopes; a database change cannot turn gateway checks into the only authorization layer.

migration_risks.name: Credential and secret posture
migration_risks.statement: BCrypt hashes, database credentials, OAuth client secrets, and signing keys must retain their storage, rotation, and non-disclosure boundaries.

workloads.name: Authentication and service authorization

workloads.business_question: Can a nominally database-light service retain its API, randomness, date, security, dependency, and observability behavior while the surrounding estate changes?

migration_risks.name: Nondeterministic output
migration_risks.statement: SecureRandom output prevents literal response comparison and requires property-based acceptance bounds.

migration_risks.name: Date contract
migration_risks.statement: The response uses LocalDate.now and therefore needs an explicit clock, timezone, and normalization policy.

migration_risks.name: API and security contract
migration_risks.statement: The endpoint shape and CloudBank read scope remain part of equivalence even when no service-owned database table is migrated.

migration_risks.name: Operational equivalence
migration_risks.statement: Health, metrics, traces, logging, failure propagation, and deployment behavior remain target acceptance concerns.
